group: layered counter with (110) prefix; halts (Coq, T4 engine from start C)
title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine, one of the holdouts of the BB(6) search, halts when started on a blank tape. The halt is a Coq theorem on busycoq's definitions. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: It halts, proved in Coq (theorem halt : halts tm c0 on busycoq's definitions, no axioms). Mirrored and with its states renamed, its table is 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1RA0LE_0LB0LF_0RA--- started in state C, one transition away from the table DeepMind proved halting in busycoq PR 93. DeepMind's fast engine, changed for that transition as for 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- (the same table started in B), reaches a halting configuration from state C after 427,055 engine steps, on a tape of about 24360 cells.

What it does. Before the halt the machine runs a layered counter: a growing prefix (110)^k is turned, at each reset, into runs of groups of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, … with large multiplicities, which the following sweeps use up. That description comes from simulation; the halt does not depend on it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 39,716 cells have been visited and 22,109 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.1).

claims.title: Prefix, groups and resets
claims.text: At each visit of the left end in state B the tape is B> 00 (110)^k (10)^a₁ 1 (10)^a₂ 1 …. Between resets k grows by 2 a visit and the sweeps merge the groups into runs of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, …; at a reset the prefix becomes about k/2 groups of size 4. Large and small resets alternate (k = 909, 37, 1670, 220, 2591, 397, 3185 between steps 3.6·107 and 5.3·108). Observed in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.48×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.48×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 12,476 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: The four rules where it departs from DeepMind's halting sibling
claims.text: For every tape on either side and every count, the four macro rules of DeepMind's engine for 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- that pass through F0 hold here in a changed form: each ends in state D with 11 more on the right instead of in state A (collision, collide, finish and defect: 10, 39, 2b+9 and 8m+39 steps).

claims.title: It halts: DeepMind's engine, changed for this table, proved in Coq
claims.text: The engine of busycoq PR 93, with the four rules that pass through F0 changed and every lemma built on them redone (the proof of 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---, retargeted to this table and start C), reaches a halting configuration from blank tape after 427,055 engine steps, on a tape of about 24360 cells. Coq 8.18.0 checks the run in one evaluation (about 4 hours); Print Assumptions halt: closed under the global context.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC0LF_0RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: It halts. For a long time it builds a run of the word 110 at the left end and turns it into groups of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, … that later sweeps use up: a counter with several levels. Underneath, it is a table one transition away from a machine DeepMind proved halting, and DeepMind's engine, changed for that transition, shows in Coq that it halts.

facts.text: A Coq theorem on busycoq's definitions; the engine needs 427,055 steps, on a tape of about 2<sup>4360</sup> cells.
Steps simulated from blank tape without a halt.
Group sizes after the sweeps, in long runs.
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: A prefix and a list of groups
html: Each time the head reaches the left end in state B, the tape reads

a prefix of k words 110, then a list of groups. Between resets the prefix grows by two words a visit, and the sweeps merge groups so that the list becomes long runs of equal sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, …; at step 2.8·108 it starts
(4^140: 140 groups of size 4 in a row).

sections.heading: The prefix becomes groups
html: When the list is used up far enough, the prefix is turned into about k/2 groups of size 4 and a new round starts. Large and small resets alternate:
The multiplicities of the sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, … act like the digits of a counter with several levels; the rule by which they carry is not worked out.

sections.heading: One transition away from a proved halt, and halting
html: This machine's table, mirrored and with its states renamed, is 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1RA0LE_0LB0LF_0RA--- started in state C; 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD--- (state B), 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC0LF_0RB--- (state D) are the same table started in the other two states. It differs in the single transition F0 from the table of 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---, which DeepMind proved halts (busycoq PR 93) with a fast engine: an evaluator over run-length tapes of macro words whose every step is proved sound in Coq. All of that engine's rules hold for this table except four, the ones that pass through F0. In those, where DeepMind's machine ends in the configuration <C 100, this one ends in <B 1 with 11 more on the right; on the digit words D n = 1 (11)^n 00 of the engine, this moves a carry from the digit on the left to the digit on the right.

We changed the engine at every place that uses one of the four rules (tools/coq/t4engine), extracted it from Coq to OCaml and checked it against direct simulation through 1.2×1010 machine steps. Run from blank tape in state C, it stops after 427,055 of its steps, on a tape of about 24360 cells, with the head in state F on a 1: a halt. The proof of the same table started in state B (holdouts/1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1LD0RE_1LA1LD_0RA0RF_0LD---/coq), which redoes DeepMind's soundness proofs for the four changed rules, needs only its table, its state map and its start changed for this machine. Coq checks the run in one evaluation, so the halt is a theorem (holdouts/1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---/coq).

sections.heading: It halts
html: The machine stops only if the head in state F reads a 1. In 109 simulated steps it never does, and the accelerated simulator saw no halt in 1.48×1014 steps. The engine run above reaches the halt much later, on a tape of about 24360 cells, so the machine runs for more than 101312 steps; the exact count is not computed.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.1).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,716 cells (26,775 left of the start, 467 right), with a density of 1s of 0.557.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Halts, proved in Coq: it is the T4 table started in C, and DeepMind's PR 93 engine changed for T4 reaches a halt after 427,055 engine steps (tape about 2^4360 cells). Before that it runs a layered counter: a growing (110)^k prefix is turned at each reset into runs of groups of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, …, which the sweeps use up (observed).
